stem: Under New Jersey law, a person may sell, solicit or negotiate insurance in the state only if the person is:
options: Licensed for the line of authority involved
Licensed in any line of authority and appointed
Registered with the commissioner for that line
Supervised by a producer licensed for that line
key: Licensed for the line of authority involved

stem: Before approving a resident individual's application for the life line, the commissioner must find that the applicant has:
options: Completed a prelicensing course in any line within five years
Served an apprenticeship with a licensed life producer
Obtained a life insurer appointment before applying
Completed a prelicensing course for the life line
key: Completed a prelicensing course for the life line

stem: A licensed producer dies suddenly. To allow time to sell the business, the commissioner may issue a temporary license under the death or disability provision to:
options: A licensed producer the clients choose

stem: A producer falsely tells a policyholder that her policy's cash value will be forfeited next year unless she surrenders it now. Which unfair trade practice is this?
An agency runs a radio ad claiming its policies "can never be cancelled for any reason," which is untrue. Which practice does this violate?
At an industry event, a producer spreads a false rumor that a competing insurer is nearly insolvent, intending to damage the insurer's reputation. This practice is called:
Several agencies agree to refuse all business with an insurer unless it raises their commissions, restraining competition in the market. This is an example of:
Two applicants are in the same risk class with equal life expectancy. The insurer charges one a higher life insurance rate because the agent dislikes the neighborhood he lives in. This is:
Under New Jersey's unfair trade practices law, an insurer may NOT refuse to issue or renew a policy because of an applicant's:
To close a life insurance sale, a producer offers to pay the client's first month's premium out of his own pocket. This is:
Which of the following is NOT treated as a rebate or unfair discrimination under New Jersey law?
options: Bonuses paid out of surplus to policyholders who buy more
Fair bonuses paid out of nonparticipating surplus
Premium abatements not specified in the contract
Surplus shares given as an inducement to buy
key: Fair bonuses paid out of nonparticipating surplus

stem: At the end of a policy year, a group life insurer readjusts the group's premium rate based on the group's loss experience. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: An illegal rebate to the group
Permitted, retroactive only for that policy year
Permitted, retroactive for up to three prior years
key: Permitted, retroactive only for that policy year

stem: Under New Jersey's unfair trade practices law, improper claim handling by an insurer is an unfair claim settlement practice when it is committed:
options: Even once, against any single claimant
With enough frequency to affect ten or more claimants
Only in ways the commissioner has published in advance
Often enough to indicate a general business practice
key: Often enough to indicate a general business practice

stem: Which of the following, done as a general business practice, is an unfair claim settlement practice in New Jersey?
options: Refusing to pay claims without a reasonable investigation
Requesting proof of death before paying a life claim
Investigating claims based on all available information
Refusing to pay a claim the policy clearly excludes
key: Refusing to pay claims without a reasonable investigation

stem: An insurer routinely sends claim payments to beneficiaries without saying which coverage each payment falls under. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Acceptable if the amount paid is correct
A violation only for health insurance claims

stem: Under New Jersey law, an insurer must keep a complete record of all complaints it has received since:
options: The start of the current calendar year
The date it was first licensed
The date five years before the current one

stem: For New Jersey's complaint record requirement, a "complaint" is defined as:
options: Any oral or written expression of dissatisfaction
Any grievance filed with the Department of Banking and Insurance
Any written request for policy information

stem: A producer shows a client an incomplete comparison that hides the surrender charges on a new annuity, to persuade her to cash in her current annuity and buy the new one. This is known as:
New Jersey's prohibition on misleading policy comparisons applies when the comparison is used to induce someone to do which of the following?
options: Pay premiums annually instead of monthly
Retain or convert an existing policy
key: Retain or convert an existing policy

stem: A producer tells a prospect that a participating policy "has paid 8% dividends every year," when similar policies actually paid far less. Under New Jersey law, this is:
An insurer markets a term life policy under the name "Retirement Savings Plan," which disguises what the product actually is. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Allowed, since product names are marketing

stem: A producer offers to give a new life insurance client half of the producer's commission on the policy. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Permitted, since the commission belongs to the producer
Allowed if the client is a family member
Allowed if the insurer approves in advance

stem: After a hearing, the commissioner finds a producer violated New Jersey's life and annuity trade practice rules without knowing, or having reason to know, it was a violation. The maximum penalty per violation is:
If a producer knew or reasonably should have known that the conduct violated New Jersey's life and annuity trade practice rules, the maximum penalty per violation is:
When the commissioner finds, after a hearing, that a person engaged in a prohibited life or annuity trade practice, the commissioner issues:
options: A desist warning with no penalty possible
An order to cease and desist
key: An order to cease and desist

stem: Before the commissioner can order a person to stop an unfair life or annuity trade practice, what must the commissioner first serve on that person?
options: A notice of hearing without any statement of charges
A statement of charges, with no hearing required
A statement of charges and notice of a hearing
A civil complaint filed in Superior Court
key: A statement of charges and notice of a hearing
